Hi Lena / Tim — thanks again for the discovery earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can make progress on the model-fit and safety evaluations you asked about.

Recap (from call)
- Use case: patient-facing triage assistant + clinician-facing summarization for intake notes.
- Priority constraints: zero PHI leakage, medically-safe refusal behavior, and hard guardrails on diagnosis / treatment suggestions.
- Success criteria: >=95% safe refusals on sensitive prompts, acceptable latency (<300ms p50) for triage flow, and no major quality regressions compared to your baseline prompts.

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Model fit: run 10k prompt set (mix of real de-identified transcripts + synthetic edge cases) across 3 model families to compare quality & cost.
   - Candidates: Redwood-v2-small (optimized, quantized), Llama-2-13B (higher factuality), and Open-7B-Chat (cost baseline).
2) Safety / refusal behavior: curated safety suite (see attached prompt_sets_v1.csv) covering PHI extraction, medical advice questions, self-harm, and adversarial jailbreaks.
3) Metrics & reporting: we'll use the attached eval_report_template.xlsx to capture refusal rates, hallucination incidents, and latency/cost per 1k tokens.

Immediate asks for next week
- Can you share a de-identified sample set (~1-2k rows) we can use to seed the eval? (we referenced de-id requirements on the call).
- Confirm stakeholders: who from Privacy/Security should be looped in for a brief intake?
- Agree a time for an evaluation run + walkthrough — I propose Tue Oct 20, 10:00-11:00 PT for a hands-on session where we run the three candidate models and review results.

Attachments: prompt_sets_v1.csv (CSV), eval_report_template.xlsx (XLSX).
Benchmarks & context: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/healthcare-models-2026
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/HS-2026-420
Drive folder (shared): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d5E-healthscope-evals

Notes on guardrails & policy behavior (short)
- We'll test explicit refusal templates and a calibrated refusal-score threshold (we provide a rubric).
- For PHI: we'll run redaction tests + prompt-based detection; if PHI detected we fallback to a generic escalation flow.
- For clinical advice: force deterministic refusal for diagnosis/treatment and provide a structured triage response (e.g., recommend clinician escalation, provide educational material only).

Next steps if that works for you: share the de-id sample by EOD Mon (Oct 19) and we'll run the eval & meet Tue at 10am PT.

Thanks — happy to adjust plan.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa / Lena — quick technical notes from the infra/serving side ahead of the Tue run: 

1) Model candidates & config- Redwood-v2-small (4-bit quantized) — likely best latency/cost tradeoff for triage flow; recommend batch size tuning and enable KV caching for multi-turn intake.
- Llama-2-13B (float16) — stronger factual coherence for clinician summarization; higher cost.
- Open-7B-Chat (int8) — low-cost baseline to validate guardrails.

2) Safety/refusal testing approach- We will run the curated safety suite from prompt_sets_v1.csv and compute: refusal_rate, false_refusal_rate (legitimate informational queries), and hallucination incidents (assertedfacts_not_in_context).
- Guardrail prompts: we'll prepend a short system-level guardrail + a refusal template. Example: "SYSTEM: You are a clinical assistant. If asked for diagnosis, medication dosing, or PHI, politely refuse and escalate to a clinician. Refusal template: 'I'm not able to provide medical advice. Please contact your care team or call 911 for emergencies.'"
- We’ll tune the refusal-score threshold to hit your target safe refusal rate while keeping false refusals under 10% on benign queries.

3) Data handling & security- For the eval run we'll operate in isolated, ephemeral workloads; logs will be access-restricted and scrubbed per your privacy guidance. If you prefer, we can run the eval on a Private deployment (VPC) — that adds an ops step but is straightforward.

4) Deliverables for Tue session- Side-by-side metrics for the three models, example failure cases, recommended guardrail prompt set, and an updated eval_report_template.xlsx pre-filled with initial results.

If you want, I can also run an initial small sweep tonight (sanity checks) once the de-id bundle is available.

—Rafael
